# Nominal cutover fixtures

The predecessor is commit `c0c4975851f34a9a2b3be8cbd3008a1f8bbafc18` (Graph 12,
TypeObject 10, interface 8, compiled unit 7, bytecode 4, Artifact 16).

`graph12-standard.lkjp` and `artifact16-standard.lkja` are the exact maintained generated bytes
from that commit, copied before changing the current implementation. Their SHA-256 values are
`3ead1a17ab28bf52ae3fcfb13b29c86352836cc328f1ec15eda079c0f3dc5b0b` and
`7ffe836adf786bcc65f66181d26cd168d5a709a18725c0d0afffd3cbf940d6ed` respectively. They prove
actual predecessor rejection, including unchanged accepted/readiness inventories on transport failure.
They are neither supported transports nor a predecessor reader.

The two `graph12-*-nominal-cutover.json` files contain fixed predecessor facts from a read-only
canonical reconstruction using the pinned predecessor Rust source. The producer serialized ordered
owner and retirement tuples, removed only generation fields, and computed BLAKE3 over their compact
JSON. It retained every exact type digest and encoded byte sequence, including dependency types.
The successor comparison additionally removes only empty record/variant parameter and constructor
argument vectors introduced by Graph 13. Nonempty vectors remain meaning. The 79 explicitly listed
new standard owners are excluded from the predecessor-owner comparison and required to exist.
All 723 prior standard owners, 2,040 application owners and retirement meanings must otherwise match.

Reproduce the input by checking out the named commit separately, opening each maintained repository
through its `GraphRepository`, reconstructing its full canonical oracle, and serializing the sorted
owner/retirement maps and canonical `encode_type_object` outputs. No compiler or runtime table enters
these expectations. The current test rederives matching facts independently from the current accepted
repositories. The older `graph10-unchanged-types-and-data.json` separately fixes monomorphic data bytes;
these fixtures do not replace it or derive expected bytes from the new codec.

`nominal-session-command.lkchg` is an authored test request derived from the copied-product
session negative witness. Its two argument placeholders select ordinary, mismatched, phantom
secret/callable and nested-secret instances. Each is first admitted as an ordinary command.
The strict-loading test changes both canonical and compiled target runners to interactive,
recomputes every affected content address and packs the documented envelope independently.
This bypasses authoring rejection while preserving a well-formed container. The ordinary control
passes strict load/deployment preparation and shutdown; the four invalid states must reject
with the session relation diagnostic before readiness. The fixture grants only isolated byte streams.
